one diagnostic rendezvous then ran with the immutable variant on echo_input.py only: both immutable job files were listed by the guest scan (poll counts 2 and 4), job A was answered with 111 and job B with 222, both tree_empty true, ordering_ok true in that diagnostic report, with 199 raw events and one pid (3696)

that run also exposed a telemetry defect: the heartbeat thread was given a detached JobLoopState, so 132 of its 199 events were heartbeat snapshots with poll_count 0 and no poll time, which the host rejects; the 67 poll_state/job events are valid and the A/B handoff is unaffected, but the raw set is not anomaly-free

the defect is fixed after the run by sharing one JobLoopState between the loop and the heartbeat and by validating a pre-first-poll heartbeat separately; the run was not repeated, so the archived raw set keeps its anomalies and is reported as such

that result is evidence that the immutable handoff works for this fixture, not proof of isolation and not authorization to switch the production transport; sandbox_rendezvous_ordering remains FAIL and the gate still refuses
revision_9_additions: the immutable decision now fails closed: any scan error (unreadable, malformed, duplicate id, conflicting sequence, filename/payload mismatch) or a truncated scan blocks all execution for that poll, even when one expected-sequence job looks valid
a valid next job beside a malformed, duplicate-id or conflicting-sequence request is not executed; no runner call and no response are produced while the blocker remains
a truncated scan never yields an executable job; the decision reports scan_truncated and the loop retries on the next poll
a transient read failure remains retryable on the next poll; permanent conditions keep blocking and must be repaired before any request is trusted
the heartbeat now shares the JobLoopState updated by the immutable loop, and a regression test proves the emitted heartbeat snapshot carries the loop's poll count and last job id
new tests bound the serve loop with max_polls for blocked-scan cases, so a fail-closed decision cannot be mistaken for a hang
